title: The dynamic landscape of the mucin-1 β subunit is altered upon the binding of a peptide mimicking mucin-1 α
abstract: The influence of the mucin-1 (Muc-1) receptor in cancer progression and its association with a poor prognosis make it a potentially ideal target in pharmacology. However, the mechanism of action and its interaction with the cellular membrane are not fully characterized at a proper atomistic level. In this contribution, using long all-atom molecular dynamics simulations largely exceeding the µs time-scale, we analyze the interaction of the membrane-embedded Muc-1 β subunit with a peptide mimicking the Muc-1 α interface. Despite showing the stability of the protein/peptide aggregate, which can be exploited for drug delivery, we also show and characterize the long-range structural modification of the transmembrane subunit upon peptide binding. This represents the first modeling of the initial alteration of the Muc-1 conformational landscape induced by the formation of the α/β heterodimer.
relevance_reason: Long all-atom MD simulations of membrane-embedded Muc-1 beta with a peptide satisfy (a)-(c) via explicit-atom dynamics applied to a biological system.

title: Predictive design of dual-atom photocatalysts for nonoxidative coupling of methane  via  a d–p orbital hybridization descriptor
abstract: Photocatalytic nonoxidative coupling of methane (NOCM) offers a mild route to C2 hydrocarbons, yet the rate-determining C–C coupling step lacks rational catalyst design principles. Using first-principles calculations, we screen 28 transition-metal dimers on C2N supports and identify Cu2/C2N, Ag2/C2N, and Au2/C2N with exceptionally low coupling barriers (0.12–0.40 eV) and robust stability. We establish a universal d–p orbital hybridization descriptor (εd − εp)—the energy difference between the metal d-band center and the methyl carbon p-band center—which exhibits a volcano-type correlation with the coupling barrier across 26 systems, peaking at εd − εp ≈ −0.42 eV in accord with the Sabatier principle. This descriptor provides a predictive framework for designing dual-atom photocatalysts for methane conversion.
relevance_reason: First-principles DFT calculations on explicit dimer/C2N atomistic models screen methane coupling barriers and derive a descriptor, satisfying (a)-(c).
